records.Name: Real-Time Partner Onboarding Sync with a Pluggable Strategy Engine
records.Tagline__c: A two-way REST integration that keeps a self-service partner sign-up platform and the CRM in sync, with versioning, ordered callouts and retries.
records.Tech_Stack__c: Apex REST, Queueable Apex, Strategy Pattern, Factory Pattern, Named Credentials, OAuth 2.0, Custom Metadata Types, Custom Permissions, Platform Events, Lightning Web Components, Lightning Data Service, HttpCalloutMock, Optimistic Versioning, JSON Merge
records.Metrics__c: 9 pluggable update strategies · 8 retry strategies over 8 ordered endpoints · 4 CRM objects updated per message
records.Business_Impact__c: Partners sign up on a self-service platform while sales teams work the same partner in the CRM, so the two sides kept drifting apart. Pratik led a real-time integration that takes every sign-up update into the CRM. It sends each relevant sales edit back to the platform as a precise, ordered update. Each change is versioned, logged and retryable, so ops teams can see what happened and fix failures with one click instead of re-keying data. Both teams now work from the same up-to-date partner record across 3 markets.
records.Technical_Deep_Dive__c:
- The entry point is an Apex REST POST. It checks a market allow-list in custom metadata, then finds the matching account, or falls back to an unconverted lead and creates one if neither exists.
- An inbound version gate applies an update only when its version is higher than the version stored on the record. Echoes of the CRM's own changes are dropped, so replays and out-of-order messages do nothing.
- A mapping layer spreads one payload across leads, accounts, opportunities, contacts and document records, and stamps the new version and the update source.
- Outbound, after-update hooks on 4 objects pass records through a relevance filter. It skips records still in error, records that are already live or approved, and updates that came from the integration itself.
- The update strategy factory returns 9 strategies behind one interface and an abstract base class. Each strategy decides for itself, using its own field map and type-aware, null-safe change detection.
- The same field maps double as the trigger's relevance filter, so change detection and payload contents can never drift apart.
- The orchestration service bulk-creates an audit record with numbered, pending requests. It enqueues callout Queueables in chunks of 5 and checks the Queueable limit before each enqueue.
- The executor runs steps in order and marks the remaining steps blocked after the first failure. Before each update it reads the current remote state and merges the change into it, so server-side file references survive.
- The version from each successful response is carried into the next step and written back to the record.
- A version conflict (HTTP 409) is retried straight away, up to 3 times. A record in error stops automatic syncs until someone retries, which prevents a pile-up of failures.
- There are two manual paths: a retry button re-sends only failed or blocked steps, and a full re-sync rebuilds all 8 endpoints from metadata through a self-chaining Queueable.
- Callouts go through Named Credentials. Human users call with their own per-user OAuth tokens. A custom permission switches automated (AI agent) users to OAuth 2.0 client credentials.
- Errors go to an external monitoring service through a platform event. Business errors (by status code) create a Task for the record owner, and a banner component warns users when the platform has overwritten their change.
- More than 50 test classes use multi-response HttpCalloutMock sequences that cover success, authorisation errors, conflicts and GET-then-PUT flows.
- Trade-off: letting each strategy decide for itself makes adding an endpoint a one-class change, but every strategy is evaluated on every trigger run.
- Trade-off: GET-merge-PUT protects remote data at the cost of two callouts per step.
records.STAR_Story__c:
Situation: Partner data was edited both on a self-service sign-up platform and in the CRM, and the two copies regularly disagreed.
Task: Build a reliable, near-real-time two-way sync that never overwrites newer data and is easy for ops to support.
Action: Pratik led the build of a versioned inbound REST service and an outbound engine with 9 pluggable update strategies, ordered Queueable callouts with read-merge-write, conflict retries and a full audit trail with manual retry tools.
Result: Updates flow both ways automatically and stale messages are ignored safely. Failures are visible, attached to the right record and fixable with one click.
records.Architecture_DSL__c:
Sign-up Platform -> Inbound REST Service : versioned update POST
Inbound REST Service -> Market Config Metadata : check market enabled
Inbound REST Service -> Update Service : process application
Update Service -> CRM Records : upsert if newer version
Inbound REST Service -> Integration Audit Log : log request/response
Inbound REST Service -> Error Monitor Event : publish errors
CRM Records -> Record Triggers : after update
Record Triggers -> Relevance Filter : drop echoes and no-ops
Relevance Filter -> Orchestration Service : changed records
Orchestration Service -> Update Strategy Factory : ask 9 strategies
Orchestration Service -> Bulk Callout Executor : enqueue chunks of 5
Bulk Callout Executor -> Sign-up Platform : GET, merge, PUT
Bulk Callout Executor -> Bulk Callout Executor : retry on 409, max 3
Bulk Callout Executor -> Integration Audit Log : status per step
Retry Button LWC -> Retry Queueable : request retry
Retry Queueable -> Sign-up Platform : re-send failed steps
CRM Records -> Conflict Warning LWC : override flag banner
records.My_Role__c: Led the integration: designed the architecture and the 9-strategy update engine, built the versioned inbound REST service and record mapping, and directed teammates who built parts of the callout, retry and credential handling.

records.Name: Business Verification (KYB/KYC) Webhooks and Follow-Up Automation
records.Tagline__c: Webhook ingestion of business and identity verification results into one canonical record, with metadata-driven mapping and automated follow-ups.
records.Tech_Stack__c: Apex REST, Batch Apex, Schedulable Apex, Custom Metadata Types, Record-Triggered Flows, Flow Orchestration, Named Credentials, OAuth 2.0, HMAC-SHA256, Custom Notifications, Email Templates, External-ID Upsert, Service Layer, Lightning Web Components
records.Metrics__c: 15 metadata-driven field mappings · 6 provider statuses mapped to 3 review states · 2 hourly follow-up batch jobs
records.Business_Impact__c: Before a partner can go live, the business and the people behind it must pass compliance checks run by a central compliance service and a third-party verification provider. Results used to arrive in ways sales couldn't easily see. Some failure reasons were lost, and partners who got stuck went unnoticed. Pratik led a webhook solution that turns every verification event into one clear record per check type, keeps a history of failure reasons, and alerts the right owner when a check is approved, rejected, stalled or never started. Sales and onboarding agents now see compliance status on the partner record and step in sooner.
records.Technical_Deep_Dive__c:
- The entry point is an Apex REST POST that the central compliance service calls. A ping header lets the caller run health checks without processing anything.
- Every event is logged with its payload, response and a step-numbered trace, so the integration audit log doubles as the event history.
- Events without a verification type are logged and skipped. All others go to an event handler that checks the market is enabled in custom metadata, then finds the partner as an account first and an unconverted lead second.
- One canonical verification record exists per partner, market and verification type, keyed by a composite external ID. Business and identity checks can pass or fail independently, and replays are idempotent.
- A field mapping service reads JSON-path, target field, data type and value map from custom metadata. Converters handle text, booleans, datetimes, lists to text and lists to multi-select.
- A missing JSON path is skipped, but a path that is present with a null value clears the field, so a resubmission removes old failure reasons.
- A status mapper in metadata turns 6 provider statuses into 3 review states, with a coded fallback if a status has no mapping.
- A rich-text failure history adds timestamped, HTML-escaped entries to the top, skips repeats of the same set and drops the oldest entries when the field is full.
- On a business error the service still writes a failure result onto the verification record, so problems are visible where users work.
- An after-save flow notifies the owner on approval or rejection, choosing email or an in-app notification by sales role.
- Two hourly batches flag checks pending for 24+ hours and sign-ups with no verification started after 24 hours. Sent-flags stop repeat alerts and are reset when a record goes back to pending.
- A separate outbound service asks the compliance service for a verification link over OAuth Named Credentials. The provider's own API is called with HMAC-SHA256-signed requests.
- Onboarding agents work verification steps as Flow Orchestration work items, and ticket creation can wait until the contract is signed in markets that use the provider.
- Tests build REST contexts directly and inject mapping rows through test-visible hooks. They cover lead fallback, one record per type, the history cap and disabled markets.
- Trade-off: the endpoint always returns HTTP 200 with a success flag, which prevents retry storms from the caller. Ordering is last-write-wins rather than compared by event time.
records.STAR_Story__c:
Situation: Compliance results for new partners were spread across systems, some failure reasons were lost, and stuck partners went unnoticed.
Task: Take verification events from the central compliance service into the CRM reliably and turn them into timely action for sales and onboarding agents.
Action: Pratik led the build of the webhook, the event handler and a metadata-driven mapping service writing to one canonical record per check type, with failure history, outcome flows and hourly follow-up batches.
Result: Each check type is tracked on its own with a full audit trail. Owners are alerted automatically when a check is approved, rejected or stalled, and new payload fields can be mapped without a code deploy.
records.Architecture_DSL__c:
Compliance Orchestrator -> Verification Webhook API : verification event
Verification Webhook API -> Integration Audit Log : log every event
Verification Webhook API -> Event Handler : events with a type
Event Handler -> Market Config Metadata : market enabled check
Event Handler -> Verification Service : resolve and upsert
Verification Service -> Field Mapping Service : apply JSON paths
Verification Service -> Status Mapper : map review status
Verification Service -> Verification Record : upsert by composite key
Verification Record -> Outcome Notify Flow : approved or rejected
Outcome Notify Flow -> Sales Owner : email or notification
Follow-up Batches -> Verification Record : find stalled checks
Follow-up Batches -> Sales Owner : delay alerts
Sales Owner -> Link Generator Service : request verify link
Link Generator Service -> Compliance Orchestrator : OAuth link request
Activation Orchestration -> Agent Work Items : verification steps
records.My_Role__c: Led the verification solution: designed the webhook, event handler, metadata-driven mapping and canonical record model, built the core ingestion, and coordinated teammates who built the provider link client, follow-up notifications and ticketing steps.

records.Name: Bulk-Safe Lead Auto-Conversion Engine with Retryable Phases
records.Tagline__c: An orchestrated engine that converts qualified self-service leads automatically, with eligibility gates, ownership rules, row locking and classified retries.
records.Tech_Stack__c: Apex, Queueable Apex, Batch Apex, Schedulable Apex, Orchestrator Pattern, Service Layer, Record Locking, Savepoints, Custom Metadata Types, Lightning Web Components, Lightning Data Service, Apex Triggers, Trigger Framework, Static Caching
records.Metrics__c: 2 re-entrant conversion phases · 5-state conversion lifecycle · 30-minute automated retry cadence
records.Business_Impact__c: Self-service sign-ups produced leads that agents had to convert into accounts and opportunities by hand once enough data arrived. This slowed onboarding and the outcome depended on who did it. Pratik built an engine that converts a lead automatically as soon as it qualifies, assigns the right owner, moves the deal to the next sales stage and retries temporary failures. Problems it can't fix go to a review queue with a clear reason, and a panel on the lead shows agents exactly what is missing. It is switched on per market through configuration.
records.Technical_Deep_Dive__c:
- A lead becomes eligible in two ways: the sign-up webhook delivers the qualifying data, or a user changes it by hand. Both run before save and share one eligibility service with exclusion rules.
- The orchestrator runs after update and acts only on records that have just become eligible, not on a Boolean flag. Its own "pending" update re-fires the trigger without queueing the work twice.
- The orchestrator applies a per-market enable flag from custom metadata. It then does one bulk status update and one Queueable enqueue, with no SOQL or DML inside loops, which is tested with 50 leads.
- The conversion service locks the leads with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, so the trigger, retry batch and UI retry can't convert the same lead twice or race on its retry counter.
- Phase A converts the lead inside a savepoint and rolls back on failure. Phase B checks the account is ready for contracting, sets record types and advances the opportunity stage in one combined update.
- Both phases can be re-run safely. A lead that is converted but not finalised goes straight to Phase B, and a lead that is already finished does nothing.
- An ownership resolver keeps a user owner, maps queue owners through metadata overrides, or falls back to a market default. Lookups are cached per transaction.
- A field validator holds about 17 pre-conversion checks plus a contracting-readiness check. It returns structured results that the LWC panel reuses, so the UI and engine never disagree.
- The error classifier treats lock contention, async and callout errors as retryable. Validation, duplicate, required-field and access errors are not, and unknown errors go to human review by default.
- A schedulable registers two offset hourly cron jobs, giving a 30-minute cadence. The retry batch re-queues retryable leads and blocks leads past the per-market maximum.
- Blocked leads go to a configured error queue with the reason stored on the record.
- One status service is the only code that writes the conversion fields. These fields are kept separate from the sign-up integration's status, and an isolation test checks the conversion never touches it.
- The LWC panel watches lead fields through Lightning Data Service, refreshes its cached Apex data when they change, and offers an async "Retry Conversion" action.
- Trade-off: retries use a fixed interval rather than exponential backoff, and some markets have no maximum. This is simple to run, but the limits have to be set deliberately.
- Trade-off: sharing one service across trigger, batch and UI removes duplicated logic, but the "converted but not finalised" state needs careful handling.
records.STAR_Story__c:
Situation: Qualified self-service leads waited for manual conversion, which delayed onboarding and gave inconsistent results.
Task: Automate conversion safely in bulk, without double conversions, wrong owners or silent failures.
Action: Pratik built an orchestrator, eligibility, ownership and validation services, a row-locked two-phase conversion service, an error classifier, a scheduled retry batch and an agent-facing LWC panel.
Result: Eligible leads convert and move forward with no manual step. Temporary failures recover on their own, and real data problems reach a review queue with an explicit reason.
records.Architecture_DSL__c:
Sign-up Webhook -> Eligibility Service : qualifying data arrives
Lead Trigger -> Eligibility Service : manual field change
Lead Trigger -> Auto-Convert Orchestrator : just became eligible
Auto-Convert Orchestrator -> Market Config Metadata : market enabled check
Auto-Convert Orchestrator -> Conversion Queueable : mark pending, enqueue
Conversion Queueable -> Conversion Service : lock rows, convert
Conversion Service -> Ownership Resolver : resolve owner
Conversion Service -> Field Validator : pre-checks
Conversion Service -> Opportunity Stage Service : advance stage
Conversion Service -> Error Classifier : classify failure
Conversion Service -> Status Service : converted or failed
Status Service -> Error Review Queue : blocked for human
Retry Scheduler -> Retry Batch : every 30 minutes
Retry Batch -> Conversion Queueable : re-queue retryable
Auto-Convert Panel LWC -> Field Validator : show checklist
Auto-Convert Panel LWC -> Conversion Queueable : manual retry
records.My_Role__c: Designed and built the whole engine end to end: the orchestrator, the eligibility, ownership, validation and status services, the two-phase conversion with row locking, the error classifier, the scheduled retries and the LWC panel.

records.Name: Two-Way Sync with an External Partner Management System
records.Tagline__c: A metadata-driven sync that applies inbound partner updates with version checks and sends CRM edits out as JSON Patch deltas, with conflict warnings.
records.Tech_Stack__c: Apex REST, Queueable Apex, Custom Metadata Types, JSON Patch, Named Credentials, OAuth 2.0, Record-Triggered Flows, Lightning Web Components, Lightning Data Service, empApi, Platform Events, Dynamic SOQL, HttpCalloutMock, Optimistic Versioning
records.Metrics__c: 5 custom metadata types drive the mapping · 3 JSON-path forms (key, index, label) · delta and full JSON Patch modes
records.Business_Impact__c: Partner details such as addresses, contacts and live status were held both in an external management system and in the CRM, and keeping them aligned took manual work. Pratik led a two-way sync. Inbound updates land on the right records automatically, and CRM edits are pushed out as small, targeted changes. New fields can be mapped through configuration instead of code. When the external system overwrites a user's failed change, the user sees a clear warning so data is checked rather than lost.
records.Technical_Deep_Dive__c:
- The inbound entry point is an Apex REST POST. It rejects empty or oversized bodies, ignores echoes of the CRM's own changes, and reads the partner ID and market through the JSON-path parser.
- Object configuration in metadata decides how the target is found: a primary object by priority with a fallback, plus child and parent objects to update in the same pass.
- A version gate applies an event only when its version is higher than the version on the primary record. It replaced an earlier timestamp check to avoid clock-skew problems.
- The JSON-path parser handles dotted keys, array indexes and label-based array lookup. Lookups are therefore independent of array order, and missing or out-of-range paths return null safely.
- Inbound mapping metadata covers target field, JSON path and data type, including one-hop relationship fields. Blank source values never clear CRM data.
- A per-record instance map merges many mappings into one update per record, applied with partial-success DML.
- A status mapping table turns a composite readiness key from the external system into the CRM's online status.
- Outbound, after-update hooks compare only fields flagged as trackable in metadata. They then enqueue a callout Queueable per batch, skipping changes made by the integration user, which prevents ping-pong loops.
- A patch builder groups mapped fields by patch path and emits sorted RFC 6902 replace operations. Changed groups are sent as a delta; lead conversion, stage changes and manual retry send the full set.
- Callouts go through Named Credentials using OAuth 2.0 client credentials. Queueables make all callouts first and do one DML at the end, which avoids uncommitted-work errors.
- Every request is logged to an audit object with a buffered debug trail, and errors also go to an external monitoring service.
- A record-triggered flow raises a conflict flag when an inbound update lands on a record whose outbound sync had failed. An LWC banner then asks the user to recheck the data.
- Dynamic SOQL uses bind variables, escaped identifiers and a validated filter clause from metadata.
- Tests inject config through test-visible overrides and mock callouts.
- Trade-off: answering HTTP 200 for business errors prevents retry storms but hides failures from the sender. An error status pauses automatic sync until a user retries from the status component.
records.Architecture_DSL__c:
Management System -> Inbound Sync API : partner update POST
Inbound Sync API -> JSON-Path Parser : extract values
Inbound Sync API -> Mapping Metadata : load config
Inbound Sync API -> Version Gate : compare versions
Version Gate -> CRM Records : apply if newer
Inbound Sync API -> Sync Audit Log : log request
Sync Audit Log -> Conflict Flag Flow : success after error
Conflict Flag Flow -> CRM Records : set overridden flag
CRM Records -> Conflict Warning LWC : show warning banner
CRM Records -> Record Triggers : after update
Record Triggers -> Change Detector : diff tracked fields
Change Detector -> Patch Queueable : enqueue delta
Patch Queueable -> Patch Builder : build JSON Patch ops
Patch Queueable -> Callout Service : send PATCH
Callout Service -> Management System : OAuth client creds
Sync Status LWC -> Callout Service : manual full resync
records.STAR_Story__c:
Situation: Partner data was duplicated between the CRM and an external management system, causing drift and manual re-keying.
Task: Build a two-way sync that is safe against stale events and loops, and configurable without code changes.
Action: Pratik led the build of a versioned inbound REST service with a generic JSON-path parser and metadata-driven mapping, plus an outbound JSON Patch engine with change detection, async callouts, audit logging and a conflict-warning UI.
Result: Updates flow both ways in near real time and stale or echoed events are ignored. Users are warned when their change may have been overwritten, and new fields need only a metadata record.
records.My_Role__c: Led the sync: designed and built the inbound REST service, version gate, JSON-path parser and metadata-driven mapping, and guided the outbound JSON Patch engine and conflict handling built with teammates.

records.Name: Eliminating Recursive-Trigger SOQL Limit Failures
records.Tagline__c: Traced and fixed "too many SOQL queries" failures caused by integration updates re-firing the full trigger and flow stack over and over.
records.Tech_Stack__c: Apex Triggers, Trigger Framework, Recursion Guards, Queueable Apex, Record-Triggered Flows, Custom Settings, Static Caching, Bulkification, Debug Log Profiling, Governor Limits, Apex Testing
records.Metrics__c: peak SOQL cut to 42 of 100 in a traced run · 4 recursion-guard patterns applied · 3 targeted fix releases
records.Business_Impact__c: Inbound partner updates and automated lead conversion started failing on the platform's 100-query limit. Partner records were left out of date and integrations errored. Pratik traced the cause to repeated small saves that each re-ran every trigger, flow and validation on the same records. He then cut that repetition with guards, merged updates and async processing. The same integration transactions now finish well within limits, which makes the onboarding flows reliable again.
records.Technical_Deep_Dive__c:
- Root cause: an integration handler made several single-record saves in one transaction, and each one re-ran the account, opportunity and contact triggers plus record-triggered flows and duplicate rules. The queries added up past the limit.
- Diagnosis used detailed debug-log profiling to count code-unit executions and running SOQL totals per trigger and flow.
- No-op DML suppression: status writes are skipped when the record already holds the target value, removing a full trigger and flow re-run.
- A per-record processed-ID set in a trigger handler re-queries and processes only records not yet handled in the transaction.
- Static Boolean re-entry guards stop cascade batches and two-way data-sync services from ping-ponging, because the trigger framework itself offers no re-entry suppression.
- Transition-based gates act only when a record has just changed state, so follow-up saves re-fire the trigger without repeating work.
- DML consolidation: record-type and stage changes after conversion became one update instead of two.
- A UI retry action that hit the limit synchronously now enqueues a Queueable and runs with its own fresh limits.
- A per-document-type query loop was replaced by one bulk query, and some heavy field-mapping logic moved into a flow.
- Entry criteria were added to a record-triggered flow so it runs only on relevant inserts or changes.
- Static, transaction-scoped caches cover market config, user and queue lookups, and environment checks. Logging skips its own work when close to the query limit.
- A hierarchy custom setting provides kill switches for triggers, validation rules, callouts and flows during data operations.
- Tests check query counts with the Limits class and run heavy scenarios in their own test contexts.
- Trade-off: static guards are cheap, but they are per transaction and need care in tests. Moving work to async fixes limits but makes results eventually consistent.
records.STAR_Story__c:
Situation: Inbound integration updates and the lead auto-conversion retry were failing with "too many SOQL queries" in a heavily automated org.
Task: Find out why and bring the transactions back inside governor limits without breaking existing automation.
Action: Pratik profiled debug logs to find the repeated trigger re-entry. He then added no-op checks, recursion and transition guards, merged updates, a bulk query, async hand-offs, flow entry criteria and static caching.
Result: The traced transaction peaked at 42 of 100 queries after the fix, and the integration and conversion flows completed reliably.
records.Architecture_DSL__c:
Inbound Webhook -> Integration Update Handler : partner update
Integration Update Handler -> No-Op DML Check : skip unchanged writes
No-Op DML Check -> Account Trigger : only real changes
Account Trigger -> Kill-Switch Setting : bypass check
Account Trigger -> Trigger Handlers : dispatch events
Trigger Handlers -> Processed-ID Guard : skip handled records
Trigger Handlers -> Transition Gate : act on state change
Transition Gate -> Async Queueables : defer heavy work
Trigger Handlers -> Record-Triggered Flows : after save
Record-Triggered Flows -> Flow Entry Criteria : filter irrelevant runs
Record-Triggered Flows -> Account Trigger : re-entry (was looping)
Integration Update Handler -> Bulk Document Query : one query for all types
Async Queueables -> Merged DML Update : one combined save
Trigger Handlers -> Static Config Cache : reuse lookups
records.My_Role__c: Diagnosed the SOQL-limit failures and built every fix, including the recursion and transition guards, the no-op checks, the merged DML, the async hand-offs, the bulk queries and the flow entry criteria.

records.Name: Delta-Based Salesforce CI/CD Pipelines with GitHub Actions
records.Tagline__c: GitHub Actions pipelines that validate pull requests with smart test selection, then promote delta deployments from staging to production.
records.Tech_Stack__c: GitHub Actions, Salesforce CLI, sfdx-git-delta, Docker, GitHub Environments, Husky, lint-staged, Prettier, ESLint, Jest, Semantic Versioning, CI/CD
records.Metrics__c: 6 workflows · 4-layer automatic test discovery · 2 environments with gated promotion
records.Business_Impact__c: Deploying a large, shared org by hand was slow and risky, and running every test on every change wasted hours. The pipelines validate each pull request against the target org, deploy only what changed and pick the right tests automatically. Production releases need an explicit, gated approval and are tagged for traceability. Teams get faster, safer releases and a clear record of what went live.
records.Technical_Deep_Dive__c:
- Pull requests to the staging branch trigger a check-only validation. Older runs for the same pull request are cancelled automatically.
- Branch names must follow a ticket or release naming convention, so every change can be traced to a work item.
- A delta tool builds a package with only the metadata changed between the base branch and HEAD. Changes with no code skip Apex validation.
- Test discovery has 4 layers: the target org's code-coverage data for changed classes, a test list in the pull request description, test classes in the delta, and a naming convention. Tests that were found but missing from the delta are added to it.
- Validation runs with the specified tests and falls back to all local tests when none are found.
- Merging to staging deploys the delta without re-running tests, because they already passed at validation, in a deploy group that never cancels a running deploy.
- Release-branch pull requests to the main branch validate against production.
- Production deploys run only by hand, only from release branches, and need a typed confirmation and a protected GitHub Environment. A dry-run option validates without deploying.
- Successful production deploys bump the patch version and create an annotated tag. A tracking workflow records a deployment and a release on merge.
- The org is authenticated with auth-URL secrets written to a temp file and deleted after login.
- Locally, pre-commit hooks run Prettier (with Apex and XML plugins), ESLint and related LWC Jest tests on staged files.
- A notification workflow posts pull request, push and pipeline results to team chat.
- Trade-off: delta deploys with targeted tests are fast but depend on accurate test discovery. A full local-test run is kept as the safety net.
- Trade-off: static analysis runs only locally, not in CI, which is a known gap.
records.Architecture_DSL__c:
Developer Commit -> Pre-commit Hooks : lint, format, jest
Developer Commit -> Feature Pull Request : open PR
Feature Pull Request -> Branch Name Check : enforce convention
Feature Pull Request -> Delta Generator : changed metadata only
Delta Generator -> Test Resolver : changed classes
Test Resolver -> Org Coverage Query : find covering tests
Test Resolver -> Validate Deployment : specified tests
Validate Deployment -> Staging Deploy Job : merge to staging
Staging Deploy Job -> Release Pull Request : promote release
Release Pull Request -> Validate Deployment : validate vs prod
Release Pull Request -> Manual Prod Deploy : typed confirmation
Manual Prod Deploy -> Release Tagging : bump version tag
Manual Prod Deploy -> Chat Notifier : deploy result
records.STAR_Story__c:
Situation: Several teams shipped to a large shared org with slow, manual and error-prone deployments.
Task: Automate validation and promotion across staging and production while keeping test runs short and releases controlled.
Action: Pratik set up GitHub Actions workflows with delta packaging, layered test discovery, environment-gated manual production deploys, release tagging and chat notifications, plus pre-commit quality hooks.
Result: Every change is validated before merge and only changed metadata is deployed. Production releases are explicit, versioned and traceable.
records.My_Role__c: Designed and built the whole pipeline setup: the validation and deployment workflows, delta packaging, layered test discovery, production gating, release tagging, notifications and pre-commit hooks.

records.Name: Production Support Tooling: Monitoring, Retries and Diagnostics
records.Tagline__c: Event-driven error monitoring, scheduled and one-click retries, and self-service diagnostics that let support fix integration failures without engineers.
records.Tech_Stack__c: Platform Events, Future Methods, Batch Apex, Schedulable Apex, Queueable Apex, Lightning Web Components, Custom Metadata Types, Custom Settings, Custom Notifications, Tasks, Anonymous Apex, Dynamic SOQL, Data Masking
records.Metrics__c: 6 automation kill-switch flags · 4 one-click retry components · event-driven, non-blocking error reporting
records.Business_Impact__c: With several real-time integrations live, failures had to be found and fixed fast, often by support staff rather than developers. The tooling reports errors to an external monitoring service without slowing down or breaking the transaction. It retries failed syncs on a schedule and gives support one-click retry buttons and a live diagnostics screen. Kill switches and a data-masking job make data loads and sandbox refreshes safe. Incidents are found sooner and most are fixed in the UI.
records.Technical_Deep_Dive__c:
- Catch blocks publish a platform event carrying the error payload. A trigger on that event sends it to an external monitoring service through an @future callout, so the main transaction is never blocked or rolled back.
- Custom metadata controls monitoring per environment: on or off, debug mode and target settings.
- Each integration writes parent and child audit records with request, response, status code, duration and a buffered step-by-step debug trail.
- An integration error logger collects errors per transaction by severity. It emails admins on critical failures and creates Tasks for record owners on business errors.
- An alternating scheduler runs two retry batches over failed ticketing-integration logs, with retry counts on both the log and the source record.
- Lead conversion and onboarding callouts have their own retry paths: a 30-minute scheduled batch and Queueables that re-send only failed or blocked steps.
- Record-page LWCs give support one-click retries for the onboarding, ticketing, conversion and management-system syncs, with toasts and live refresh.
- A diagnostics LWC starts a test sync and polls the audit records live, showing the running user, credential, endpoint and each step's status.
- Anonymous Apex runbooks check API access for integration users, test outbound credentials and publish test events for message-bridge checks.
- A hierarchy custom setting provides kill switches for triggers, validation rules, callouts, flows and assignment during data operations.
- A generic data-masking batch builds dynamic queries and replaces chosen fields with type-safe placeholder values for sandboxes.
- Logging is limit-aware and skips its own monitoring when close to the query limit, so diagnostics can't cause the next failure.
- Trade-off: asynchronous error reporting keeps transactions safe but can lose an event if the callout fails. Tasks and audit records act as the durable backup.
records.STAR_Story__c:
Situation: Several live integrations failed now and then, and fixing them needed a developer to read logs and replay data.
Task: Make failures visible straight away and let support resolve most of them on their own.
Action: Pratik built event-driven error reporting, audit logging, scheduled retry batches, one-click retry LWCs, a live diagnostics screen, ops runbook scripts, kill switches and a masking batch.
Result: Failures appear in monitoring and on the affected record. Most are retried automatically or with one click, and developers are pulled in only for real defects.
records.My_Role__c: Designed and built all of the support tooling: event-driven error reporting, audit logging, the retry batches and one-click retry components, the diagnostics screen, the ops runbooks, the kill switches and the data-masking job.

records.Name: Automatic Address Geocoding for Leads and Accounts
records.Tagline__c: A trigger-driven geocoding service that turns partner addresses into map coordinates, switching between Queueable and Batch by volume, with failure flagging.
records.Metrics__c: 2 objects geocoded automatically · 2 async paths picked by volume · 3 settings in custom metadata
records.Tech_Stack__c: Apex, Apex Triggers, Queueable Apex, Batch Apex, REST Callouts, JSON Parsing, Custom Metadata Types, Custom Settings, Geolocation Fields, Service Layer, HttpCalloutMock, Partial-Success DML
records.Business_Impact__c: Sales and operations teams needed accurate map coordinates for every partner, both for planning and for systems further down the line. Typing them in by hand was slow and often wrong. Pratik built a service that geocodes a lead or account automatically when it is created or its address changes. It scales from single edits to bulk data loads, and flags any address it can't resolve so someone can fix it. A companion batch fills in missing trading-address fields from the existing address, so older records are complete too.
records.Technical_Deep_Dive__c:
- The entry points are the after-insert and after-update handlers on leads and accounts. They are gated by a callout kill switch in a hierarchy custom setting, so data loads can turn geocoding off.
- A helper keeps only records whose country is enabled in custom metadata, so geocoding can be switched on per market without code.
- On update, a record is sent for geocoding only if a relevant address field actually changed. This avoids repeat callouts and loops with the coordinate write-back.
- On insert, records that already get coordinates elsewhere are skipped: leads from the self-service sign-up feed and accounts created by lead conversion.
- A minimum-address check (city plus country or postcode) stops callouts that can't succeed.
- A volume switch reads a threshold from custom metadata. Small sets go to a Queueable with callouts; larger sets go to a Batch with a configurable scope size, which keeps each transaction within callout limits.
- Both async paths share one processing utility. It formats the address, calls the geocoding API, parses the first result's location and writes latitude and longitude to a geolocation field.
- When an address can't be resolved, or an error occurs, a failure flag is set on the record instead of failing the job, so bad addresses can be found with a simple report.
- The utility returns processed, success and failure counts, which the stateful batch logs when it finishes.
- The callout uses a short timeout and URL-encodes the address, and the API URL comes from metadata.
- A separate backfill batch copies standard address parts into empty trading-address fields per object and market. Its query is configurable and it uses partial-success DML.
- Tests use HttpCalloutMock for success and failure responses. They cover the Queueable, Batch and handler paths for both objects, plus empty input and unsupported object types.
- Trade-off: choosing Queueable or Batch by volume keeps small edits fast and bulk loads safe, at the cost of two code paths.
- Trade-off: flagging failures instead of retrying keeps the design simple and visible, but needs someone to fix flagged addresses.
records.STAR_Story__c:
Situation: Partner records needed accurate coordinates, but they were entered by hand or missing, especially after bulk imports.
Task: Geocode leads and accounts automatically and reliably at any volume, without hitting governor limits or making pointless callouts.
Action: Pratik built a trigger-driven service with change detection, market filtering in metadata, an async path chosen by volume (Queueable or Batch), a shared processing utility, failure flagging and a trading-address backfill batch.
Result: New and changed addresses get coordinates automatically, bulk loads are handled safely, and addresses that can't be resolved are flagged for review.
records.My_Role__c: Designed and built the whole geocoding service end to end: the trigger integration, change detection, the async path chosen by volume, the processing utility, failure flagging, the address backfill batch and the tests.
records.Architecture_DSL__c:

Lead and Account Triggers -> Market Filter Metadata : market enabled?
Lead and Account Triggers -> Geocode Service : candidate records
Geocode Service -> Address Validator : changed and complete
